text:
Use stars-and-bars with inclusion–exclusion.

Without upper bounds, the number of nonnegative integer solutions to

\[
x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4=20
\]

is

\[
\binom{20+4-1}{4-1}=\binom{23}{3}=1771.
\]

Now exclude solutions where some \(x_i\ge 8\). Let \(A_i\) be the set where \(x_i\ge 8\). Put \(y_i=x_i-8\ge 0\). If \(k\) variables are forced to be at least \(8\), the remaining sum is \(20-8k\), giving

\[
\binom{20-8k+3}{3}
\]

solutions, provided \(20-8k\ge 0\).

By inclusion–exclusion:

\[
\begin{aligned}
N&=\binom{23}{3}
-\binom41\binom{15}{3}
+\binom42\binom{7}{3}\\
&=1771-4\cdot455+6\cdot35\\
&=1771-1820+210\\
&=\boxed{161}.
\end{aligned}
\]

The \(k=3\) term vanishes since \(20-24<0\).

Quick check: setting \(y_i=7-x_i\) transforms the problem into \(y_1+y_2+y_3+y_4=8\) with \(0\le y_i\le 7\). There are \(\binom{11}{3}=165\) unrestricted solutions, and exactly \(4\) violate a bound (one \(y_i=8\), the rest \(0\)), giving \(165-4=161\).
